commons.title: Finnish Tatar soldiers - Semiulla Wafin (cropped).jpg
commons.description:
Finnish Tatar soldiers on leave for the Bayram in 1941. 
In picture (from left) sitting: Jarulla Alautdin, Naim Nasibullen, Letfulla Baibulat, Fatih Bedretdin. Standing: Abdulhak Asis, Haider Alautdin, Zinnetulla Hakim, Semiulla Wafin, Haider Asis, Abdul-Hamid Bedretdin, Semiulla Hakim.  

Some surnames have had different versions either before or after this time. For example Nasibullen: Nasibulla, Nasib and Hakim: Hakimdshan.
commons.editorial_reason: Identified Finnish Tatars are shown in ordinary military uniforms; no visible traditional dress or cultural practice.

commons.title: Idel-Ural State memorial service in Poland.jpg
commons.description: As part of the memorial service marking the 20th anniversary of the Idel-Ural State, Tatars are marching along the main street in Warsaw to lay flower wreaths for the deceased Muslims. The ribbon reads: "From the Turk-Tatars of Idel-Ural to the victims of the struggle for the independence of Poland". The memorial service was organized by Ayaz Ishaki. It was attended also by seven Finnish Tatars: Fatih Arat, Letfulla Baibulat, Aisa Hakimcan, Gibadulla Murtasin, Ymär Sali, Ahmedcan Samaletdin and Safa Hamidulla.
commons.editorial_reason: Tatars are visibly marching in a memorial service, and the caption specifically identifies Finnish Tatar participants.

commons.description: Politician Sadri Maksudi (Arsal) with Finnish Tatars in Tampere, year 1920. In first row: Semiulla Wafa (young boy), Camal Baibulat, Kamal Baibulat, Sadri Maksudi, Camal babay Yosıf, İmad Camal; standing Abbas Bedretdin, Aisa Hakimcan, Zinnetulla Wafa, Bilal Kadir, Husein Numan, Ahmetcan Camaletdin, Husein Camaletdin. (Names originally written in Tatar Arabic alphabet).
commons.editorial_reason: Group portrait of Finnish Tatars in ordinary clothing, with no visible traditional dress or other cultural content.
